evidence.intree_statement: Class Terminal := { terminal_obj : C; one {x} : x ~> terminal_obj; one_unique {x} (f g : x ~> terminal_obj) : f ≈ g }.   (* Awodey's clause (1): a distinguished 1 with !_C, every f : C ~> 1 equal to it *)

Class Cartesian := { product_obj : obj → obj → obj where "x × y" := (product_obj x y); fork {x y z} (f : x ~> y) (g : x ~> z) : x ~> y × z; exl {x y} : x × y ~> x; exr {x y} : x × y ~> y; fork_respects : ∀ x y z, Proper (equiv ==> equiv ==> equiv) (@fork x y z); ump_products {x y z} (f : x ~> y) (g : x ~> z) (h : x ~> y × z) : h ≈ fork f g ↔ (exl ∘ h ≈ f) * (exr ∘ h ≈ g) }.

Corollary exl_fork {x z w : C} (f : x ~> z) (g : x ~> w) : exl ∘ f △ g ≈ f.   [line 220] Corollary exr_fork ... : exr ∘ f △ g ≈ g.   [line 261] Corollary fork_exl_exr {x y : C} : exl △ exr ≈ @id _ (x × y).   (* precisely Awodey's three product equations, derived from ump_products *)

Class Closed := { exponent_obj : obj → obj → obj where "y ^ x" := (exponent_obj x y); exp_iso {x y z} : x × y ~> z ≊ x ~> z^y; curry' {x y z} : x × y ~> z → x ~> z^y := to (@exp_iso x y z); uncurry' {x y z} : x ~> z^y → x × y ~> z := from (@exp_iso x y z); eval' {x y} : y^x × x ~> y := @uncurry' _ _ _ id; ump_exponents' {x y z} (f : x × y ~> z) : eval' ∘ first (@curry' _ _ _ f) ≈ f }.

Corollary curry_uncurry {x y z} (f : x ~> z^y) : curry (uncurry f) ≈ f.   [line 141] Corollary eval_first {x y z : C} (f : x ~> z^y) : eval ∘ first f ≈ uncurry f.   (* together these give Awodey's second exponential equation (ε ∘ (g × 1_A))~ = g, since curry (eval ∘ first g) ≈ curry (uncurry g) ≈ g *)
Definition first {x y z : C} (f : x ~> y) : x × z ~> y × z := f ∘ exl △ exr.   (* Awodey's g × 1_A := ⟨g p1, p2⟩, verbatim *)

Proposition CartesianProductIsUniversalProperty : IsUniversalProperty C^op (fun z => IsCartesianProduct x y z) (fun z => CartesianProductStructuresEquiv x y z).   (* identifies the operations-and-equations predicate IsCartesianProduct with the representability iso Hom(−,z) ≅ Hom(−,x) × Hom(−,y): the one clause of Prop 6.12 for which the equational⇔UMP equivalence IS proved in-tree *)

statement_record.book: A category C is cartesian closed if and only if it carries the following operations-and-equations structure: (1) an object 1 with !_C : C → 1 such that every f : C → 1 equals !_C; (2) for each A,B an object A × B with p1, p2 and, for each f : Z → A, g : Z → B, an arrow ⟨f,g⟩ satisfying p1⟨f,g⟩ = f, p2⟨f,g⟩ = g and ⟨p1 h, p2 h⟩ = h; (3) for each A,B an object B^A with ε : B^A × A → B and, for each f : Z × A → B, a transpose f~ : Z → B^A satisfying ε ∘ (f~ × 1_A) = f and (ε ∘ (g × 1_A))~ = g, where g × 1_A := ⟨g p1, p2⟩. The proof is routine and left to the reader.
statement_record.intree: Class Terminal := { terminal_obj : C; one {x} : x ~> terminal_obj; one_unique {x} (f g : x ~> terminal_obj) : f ≈ g }.  /  Class Cartesian := { product_obj; fork; exl; exr; fork_respects; ump_products {x y z} (f : x ~> y) (g : x ~> z) (h : x ~> y × z) : h ≈ fork f g ↔ (exl ∘ h ≈ f) * (exr ∘ h ≈ g) }.  /  Class Closed := { exponent_obj; exp_iso {x y z} : x × y ~> z ≊ x ~> z^y; ...; ump_exponents' {x y z} (f : x × y ~> z) : eval' ∘ first (curry' f) ≈ f }.

evidence.intree_statement: Inductive Ty : Set := | TyUnit : Ty (* unit type: terminal object *) | TyPair : Ty → Ty → Ty (* product type: categorical product *) | TyArrow : Ty → Ty → Ty. (* arrow type: exponential / hom *)   (* header line 20: 'There are no extra base types: [TyUnit] is the only ground type' *)

Inductive Exp Γ : Ty → Set := | EUnit : Exp Γ TyUnit | Pair {τ1 τ2} : Exp Γ τ1 → Exp Γ τ2 → Exp Γ (TyPair τ1 τ2) | Fst {τ1 τ2} : Exp Γ (TyPair τ1 τ2) → Exp Γ τ1 | Snd {τ1 τ2} : Exp Γ (TyPair τ1 τ2) → Exp Γ τ2 | VAR {τ} : Var Γ τ → Exp Γ τ | LAM {dom cod} : Exp (dom :: Γ) cod → Exp Γ (dom ⟶ cod) | APP {dom cod} : Exp Γ (dom ⟶ cod) → Exp Γ dom → Exp Γ cod.

Inductive Step : ∀ {Γ τ}, Exp Γ τ → Exp Γ τ → Set := ... | ST_FstPair Γ τ1 τ2 (v1 : Exp Γ τ1) (v2 : Exp Γ τ2) : ValueP v1 → ValueP v2 → Fst (Pair v1 v2) ---> v1 | ST_SndPair ... Snd (Pair v1 v2) ---> v2 | ST_Beta Γ dom cod (e : Exp (dom :: Γ) cod) (v : Exp Γ dom) : ValueP v → APP (LAM e) v ---> SubExp {|| v ||} e | ...   (* the only in-tree relation on terms; call-by-value, no surjective pairing, no eta *)

#[export] Program Instance Exp_Setoid {Γ dom cod} : Setoid (Exp Γ (dom ⟶ cod)) := { equiv := λ f g, ∀ E, SemExp f E ≈ SemExp g E }.   (* the equality actually used: agreement of denotations in the standard model, not provability in the calculus *)

statement_record.book: A typed lambda-calculus consists of TYPES built from basic types and closed under A × B and A → B; TERMS, namely variables of each type, possibly typed constants, and the formation rules ⟨a,b⟩ : A × B, fst(c) : A, snd(c) : B, application c a : B, abstraction λx.b : A → B; and EQUATIONS between terms: fst⟨a,b⟩ = a, snd⟨a,b⟩ = b, ⟨fst(c), snd(c)⟩ = c (surjective pairing), (λx.b)a = b[a/x] (beta), and λx. c x = c when x does not occur in c (eta).
statement_record.intree: Inductive Ty : Set := TyUnit | TyPair : Ty → Ty → Ty | TyArrow : Ty → Ty → Ty.   /   Inductive Exp Γ : Ty → Set := EUnit | Pair | Fst | Snd | VAR | LAM | APP.   /   Inductive Step : ∀ {Γ τ}, Exp Γ τ → Exp Γ τ → Set := ... ST_FstPair (values only) | ST_SndPair (values only) | ST_Beta (value argument only) | congruence rules.
statement_record.strength_comparison: syntax: same (all seven term formers and both type formers, in intrinsically-typed de Bruijn form with typing built into the GADT). equations: intree-weaker in three specific ways. (a) No basic types and no typed constants — TyUnit is the only ground type, so the in-tree calculus is over the empty signature, whereas Awodey's definition takes arbitrary basic types and constants (the sibling files' vestigial `HostExprsSem A` context, Instance/Lambda.v:134-135, is documented at lines 52-56 as an unused extension point). (b) There is no equational theory at all: the only term relation is a CALL-BY-VALUE small-step reduction, in which ST_FstPair/ST_SndPair are restricted to value components and ST_Beta to a value argument, so it does not even contain Awodey's fst/snd/beta equations at arbitrary terms, and it contains neither surjective pairing ⟨fst c, snd c⟩ = c nor eta λx. c x = c. statement_record.book: For a lambda-calculus L, the category of types C(L) has as objects the types of L; as arrows A → B the equivalence classes [c] of closed terms c : A → B, where [a] = [b] iff the equation a = b is provable in L; identity 1_A = [λx.x]; and composition c ∘ b = λx. c (b x). It is a well-defined category with binary products from the product types and pairing/projections, and a terminal object is easily added.

statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on exactly the quotient. Objects (Ty), identity (λx.x) and composition (λx. f (g x)) are Awodey's verbatim, and the promised structure is delivered — products via TyPair with pairing/Fst/Snd (Lambda_Cartesian:252) and the terminal object Awodey says is 'easily added' (Lambda_Terminal:242). But the hom-setoid is DENOTATIONAL: f ≈ g means SemExp f and SemExp g agree on every environment in the standard model, not that the equation f = g is provable in L; the file itself states the consequence at lines 93-96, 'with [TyUnit] the only base type, the standard model identifies more terms than βη-conversion does. It follows that [Lambda Γ] is the image of the syntactic category inside the standard model, not the free cartesian closed category of Lambek's theorem on the nose.' Second difference: homs are Exp Γ (A ⟶ B), i.e. OPEN terms in a fixed ambient context Γ, rather than closed terms; Γ := [] would recover closed terms but is never taken. Nothing in-tree is stronger than the book here.

statement_record.book: The category of types C(L) of any lambda-calculus L is cartesian closed: exponentials are the function types B^A := A → B, evaluation is ε = λz. fst(z) snd(z) : B^A × A → B, and the transpose of f : Z × A → B is f~ = λz λx. f⟨z,x⟩ : Z → B^A. The two equations of Prop 6.12 — ε ∘ (f~ × 1_A) = f and (ε ∘ (g × 1_A))~ = g — are verified by explicit lambda-calculus computation using α × β = λw. ⟨α fst(w), β snd(w)⟩.
